title: Daryl Bem's backward causality study and failed replications

tellings.quote: the replication crisis started in 2010 with Daryl Beam's research on the backward causality, that's how it began.

plain: A Cornell psychologist named Daryl Bem published a paper in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology reporting evidence of backward causality, the idea that a future event can affect what people do now, and other researchers, among them Ray Hyman, Richard Wiseman and Stuart Ritchie, tried and failed to get the same results. The skeptic Michael Shermer tells Michels this as a researcher, saying "the replication crisis started in 2010" with Bem's work, meaning the wider discovery that many findings in psychology do not hold up when repeated. He also mentions that the study drew attention as far as Stephen Colbert's show.
